<p>This past summer, I interned at Dasion as a Software Engineer and Machine Learning Intern based in Claremont, California. Dasion is a data-driven company focused on leveraging machine learning to support medical and behavioral research. My role placed me at the intersection of software engineering and applied machine learning, where I worked on developing tools to support emotion recognition in children using medical imaging data.</p>

<p>Working on a project with real clinical implications pushed me to think carefully about model selection, data quality, and the downstream impact of engineering decisions. Every preprocessing step, every architecture choice, and every evaluation metric carried weight — because the end users were researchers and practitioners working with vulnerable populations.</p>

<p>One of the most exciting aspects of this internship was building an emotion-based music recommender using the Spotify API — a creative application that connected the emotional state detected by our models to curated playlists, demonstrating the real-world potential of the system beyond clinical settings.</p>
